presentation.title: Bank fraud alert
presentation.summary: Practice responding to an unexpected bank text, a pressure call, a fake website, and a security-code request.
presentation.practiceGoal: Recognize urgency, switch to a trusted contact method, and protect account credentials and security codes.

warningSigns.sign: An unexpected alert creates fear about losing money.
A message includes a link and asks you to act immediately.
A caller asks you to move money to protect it.
Someone asks for a one-time security code.

finalReview.safestAction: End the conversation and contact the bank using the number on your card, statement, or official app.

realWorldActions.action: Do not reply to the message or use its link.
Call the bank through a number you already trust.
Never share a one-time security code with a caller.
If you shared information, contact the bank immediately and change affected passwords.

artifact.heading: Suspicious charge alert
artifact.message: BANK ALERT: Suspicious charge of $1,248.50 at Target. Reply YES if this was you, NO to speak with Fraud Prevention. Or use bank-secure-review.example to dispute this yourself.
artifact.transcript: A text claims there is a suspicious charge of $1,248.50. It asks for a reply or offers a link to dispute the charge.

scene.question: How would you check whether this alert is real?
scene.description: Choose the first action you would take.

warningSigns.sign: The message was unexpected.
It creates urgency around a large amount of money.
It asks you to reply or use a link supplied in the message.

choice.title: Reply NO by text
choice.subtitle: Continue the conversation using the number that contacted you.

feedback.heading: The scammer still controls the conversation
feedback.consequence: Replying may confirm that your number is active and can lead to a convincing pressure call.
feedback.explanation: A safer verification starts through a contact method you choose yourself, not one supplied by the alert.

warningSigns.sign: The sender controls the reply channel.
A reply can lead to more urgent contact.

choice.title: Use the link in the text
choice.subtitle: Open the page supplied by the alert to dispute the charge.

feedback.heading: Unexpected links can lead to imitation websites
feedback.consequence: The link can open a fake bank page designed to collect passwords and personal information.
feedback.explanation: Scammers copy familiar branding and use look-alike web addresses. Open the saved bank app or type a trusted address instead.

warningSigns.sign: The link arrived without being requested.
The address does not match a known bank website.

choice.title: Contact the bank independently
choice.subtitle: Open the official app or call the number printed on your card.

feedback.heading: You changed to a trusted channel
feedback.consequence: You can check the account without relying on information supplied by the sender.
feedback.explanation: Choosing the contact method yourself breaks the scammer's control and gives you time to verify the claim.

warningSigns.sign: The alert supplied its own contact route.
The message tried to rush the verification.

artifact.heading: Your account is being drained
artifact.message: We see a hacker trying to empty your account. To protect your money, transfer it to a temporary government safe vault immediately.
artifact.transcript: The caller says hackers are draining the account and insists that the money must be transferred to a temporary government safe vault right now.

scene.question: What would you do while the caller is pressuring you?
scene.description: The caller sounds calm and professional, but insists there is no time to wait.

warningSigns.sign: The caller creates an emergency.
The caller asks for an immediate money transfer.
The caller discourages time to verify the claim.

choice.title: Agree to transfer the money
choice.subtitle: Follow the caller's instructions to move the funds.

feedback.heading: Banks do not use secret safe-vault transfers
feedback.consequence: Money sent under the caller's direction may go directly to an account controlled by the scammer.
feedback.explanation: Urgency and unusual transfer instructions are strong signs to end the call and verify independently.

warningSigns.sign: A request to move money to keep it safe.
Pressure to complete the transfer immediately.

choice.title: Hang up and call the bank yourself
choice.subtitle: Use the number printed on the back of your debit card.

feedback.heading: You ended the pressure and chose a trusted number
feedback.consequence: The real bank can check the account without the suspicious caller remaining involved.
feedback.explanation: Hanging up creates time to think and prevents the caller from guiding each next action.

warningSigns.sign: The caller wanted to keep you on the line.
The caller supplied an unusual solution.

choice.title: Ask the caller to prove their identity
choice.subtitle: Keep the call active while asking for employee details.

feedback.heading: A scammer can prepare convincing details
feedback.consequence: The caller can provide a fake name, employee number, or information gathered about you.
feedback.explanation: Information supplied by the caller cannot independently verify the caller. End the call and contact the bank yourself.

warningSigns.sign: The same caller supplies both the claim and the proof.
The pressure continues while you try to verify.

artifact.heading: Bank Account Verification
artifact.message: To stop the suspicious charge, verify your full identity immediately.
artifact.transcript: The page asks for a username, password, and full Social Security number. The web address came from an unexpected text and does not match a known bank address.

outcome.label: Account information at risk
outcome.heading: The link led to a phishing page
outcome.explanation: The imitation page requests account credentials and personal information.

warningSigns.sign: The page was opened from an unexpected text.
The domain is unfamiliar.
The page asks for several sensitive details at once.

artifact.heading: Official account check
artifact.message: You open the official banking app yourself. The balance is correct and no suspicious charge appears.
artifact.transcript: The official banking app shows that the account is fine. The alert did not come from the bank.

outcome.label: Account protected
outcome.heading: You verified the alert safely
outcome.explanation: You used an official channel and confirmed that the unexpected alert was false.

warningSigns.sign: The original message did not match the information in the official app.
The sender tried to direct the verification process.

artifact.heading: A security code is requested
artifact.message: I started the secure transfer. I am texting you a verification code. Read it out loud so I can finalize the security vault.
artifact.transcript: The caller says a transfer is underway and asks the learner to read a new verification code aloud.

scene.question: What would you do when the caller asks for the code?
scene.description: A text arrives while the caller remains on the line.

warningSigns.sign: The caller asks for a one-time code.
The caller claims the code is needed to protect money.
The caller keeps the conversation moving quickly.

choice.title: Read the code aloud
choice.subtitle: Give the caller the number so the transfer can continue.

feedback.heading: A security code can unlock the account
feedback.consequence: The scammer may use the code to sign in, approve a transfer, or bypass account protection.
feedback.explanation: One-time codes are intended only for the account owner. A legitimate employee should not ask you to read one aloud.

warningSigns.sign: A caller requests a one-time code.
The code is tied to a transfer you did not initiate.

choice.title: Read the full text before speaking
choice.subtitle: Pause and check what the security-code message actually says.

feedback.heading: You paused long enough to see the warning
feedback.consequence: Reading the full message can reveal that the code must never be shared.
feedback.explanation: Slowing the conversation interrupts the scammer's pressure and gives written warnings a chance to help.

warningSigns.sign: The caller tries to make you act before reading.
The request involves a private security code.

artifact.heading: Security code: 994-123
artifact.message: Bank employees will NEVER ask for this code over the phone. Do not share it.
artifact.transcript: The security message says bank employees will never ask for this code over the phone and instructs the recipient not to share it.

scene.question: What would you do after reading the warning?
scene.description: The caller is still waiting for an answer.

warningSigns.sign: The text directly contradicts the caller.
The caller is asking for a code marked private.

choice.title: Hang up and call the real bank
choice.subtitle: Use the official fraud number from your card or statement.

feedback.heading: You protected the code and changed channels
feedback.consequence: The scammer cannot use the code, and the real bank can help check the account.
feedback.explanation: Security codes should stay private. Ending the call prevents further pressure or requests.

warningSigns.sign: The caller ignored a clear security warning.
The caller requested private authentication information.

choice.title: Trust the caller and share the code
choice.subtitle: Assume the caller is an exception to the written warning.

feedback.heading: The written warning applies to every caller
feedback.consequence: The code may allow the scammer to complete an account sign-in or money transfer.
feedback.explanation: A caller's confidence or urgency does not override the security instruction in the message.

warningSigns.sign: The caller asks you to ignore a security warning.
The request gives someone else access to authentication.

artifact.heading: Trusted contact restored
artifact.message: You ended the suspicious conversation and contacted the bank through an official channel.
artifact.transcript: The suspicious conversation ends. The learner contacts the bank using a trusted number.

outcome.label: Scam stopped
outcome.heading: You protected the account
outcome.explanation: You ended the suspicious conversation and contacted the bank through an official channel.

warningSigns.sign: The caller created urgency.
The caller requested unusual transfers or private codes.

artifact.heading: Security code shared
artifact.message: The scammer uses the code to bypass account protection and gain access.
artifact.transcript: After receiving the one-time code, the scammer can bypass two-factor authentication and compromise the account.

outcome.label: Account compromised
outcome.heading: The scammer gained access
outcome.explanation: The scammer used the code to bypass two-factor authentication and compromise the account.

warningSigns.sign: The caller requested a one-time security code.
The caller claimed normal security rules did not apply.

command.displayText: BANK ALERT: Suspicious charge of $1,248.50 at Target. Reply YES if this was you, or NO to speak with Fraud Prevention. Or click the link to dispute this yourself.

option.text: Click the link in the text
Ignore the text and log into the official banking app

command.displayText: The link opens a fake banking portal asking for your username, password, and Social Security number. This is a phishing trap.
You open the official banking app yourself. Your real balance is fine and no pending charge exists. Scam defeated.

The caller says: Thank you for responding. We see a hacker actively attempting to drain your account. To secure your funds, we need to move them to a temporary FDIC-secured government safe vault immediately.

option.text: Hang up and call the number on the back of your debit card
Ask the caller to verify their employee identity

command.displayText: The caller says: I have initiated the secure transfer to protect your money. I am texting you a verification code right now. Read it out loud so I can finalize the security vault.

option.text: Read the code out loud to the caller
Read the text message carefully before speaking

command.displayText: The text says: Security Code: 994-123. Bank employees will NEVER ask for this code over the phone. Do not share it.

option.text: Realize it is a scam, hang up, and call the bank fraud line
Trust the caller anyway and give them the code

command.displayText: Win condition: You stopped the scam and contacted the bank through an official channel.
Critical loss: The scammer used the code to bypass two-factor authentication and compromise the account.
